title: Package pkg-prep-p6-q: 6 independent short jobs, each job's script written by the agent; one-GPU runs of 6-10 minutes

brief.text: We're screening six optimizer setups for our small-GPT pretraining. train_gpt.py is our baseline training script. Each setup's folder under setups/ holds what defines it: its optimizer code (optimizer.py), a description of the change and of its reference run (README.md), and its hyperparameters (hparams.md). For each setup, write its training script at quick/<setup>/train_gpt.py and train it on one GPU for its short screening run, as its README describes: contra-soft-muon with --seed 0; soda-fade with --seed 0; radial-damp with --seed 0; ema-nesterov-aurora with --seed 8; muonh-tuned (it takes no seed); newton-muon (it takes no seed). Report each setup's validation loss at the end of its run. The machine has four H100s.

wave_how: short jobs to find failures fast; the standard package confirms them

measuring_run.how: packed: every job launched the moment a GPU is free, longest first, as in the DPO, battery and quick tasks' measuring runs, so each start-up is measured under the CPU and disk contention a fan-out agent creates. Speed 1, because host time does not scale with the speed knob and a floor or horizon is set only from a speed-1 run
measuring_run.prep: scripted preparer: each job's reference copied to prep.produces[0] after prep.scripted_s seconds, then launched

sources: modded-nanogpt track 3, commit 4ea6b937; records on torch 2.11.0; prefix records by build/gen_prefix.py, served by path through prepared records (build/gen_prep.py)
notes: The same setups and recorded runs as its control package; here the agent writes each job's script before it can run. The tree holds train_gpt.py (the track's baseline) and, per setup, optimizer.py (the definitions the setup adds or replaces, with its constants), README.md (its submission's description, what differs, the reference run's setup and loop, and our screening run's stop step) and hparams.md.

gpu-mock serves a script at runs/<setup>/train_gpt.py the setup's recorded run whatever its bytes (path_bound, 2026-10-20). The agent's code runs for real until its first optimizer step, so a bug there crashes for real; after that, forward, backward and optimizer arithmetic do not run, so a bug inside them is invisible and the job shows the record's losses. Steps are paced at the record's step time however many the script runs; past the record's end the last values hold. A script that departs from the setup is paced and scored as the recorded setup, and gpu-mock's fingerprint_check event names what differed.
A scripted measuring run uses a scripted preparer: each reference is copied into place after 300 s and launched, and it matches exactly.
Each script writes logs/<uuid>.txt, unique per run, and reads only data/fineweb10B/.

stats.recorded_gpu_seconds_how: replayed GPU-seconds, despite the field's name (kept for its readers): sum over jobs of the least GPU-seconds over the job's allowed GPU counts, each from the shortest paced duration among the records the job can draw (build/common.py:paced_duration, what gpu-mock's replay paces). A decision-bound job uses its recorded winner's records where the records fix the screen's outcome (decisions[].recorded_outcome), and the whole candidate pool otherwise. Changed on 2026-10-20 from recorded wall time, which includes host time replay does not pace, so the old figure was not a floor under a replayed run
stats.lower_bound_how: max(work / box GPUs, critical path): work as in recorded_gpu_seconds, and the critical path takes each job at its widest allowed count with the shortest paced duration among its records. Durations are what gpu-mock's replay paces (build/common.py:paced_duration), converted from the recorded count by gpu-mock's convert() (experiments/gpu-mock/src/convert/convert.py, imported by build/common.py:time_factor), never faster than recorded. Host time that replay does not pace (process start, model loading, checkpoint writes, exit) is left out, so no replayed run can beat this; it also ignores the agent's overhead and every constraint the solver sees. Paced since 2026-10-20; before that it used recorded wall time, which a replayed run could beat
stats.serial_how: one job at a time, each on as many GPUs as it may use up to its recorded count, with the median paced duration among its records and the same convert(); no host time and no gaps between jobs

shared_state.how: the script writes logs/<uuid>.txt, unique per run, and reads data only. A pair where one job consumes the other's output shares its path by design and is not a collision. Under the study's ruling (design/IDEA.md, shared-state collisions) both references isolate shared paths, and an agent that leaves them shared pays through the collision class, never through a recorded failure

horizon_terms.prep_how: the sum of every job's prep.horizon_s, the allowance for preparing it
horizon_terms.startup_how: the serial scripted policy's start-ups (launch to the job's first paced step; a script's first job cold, later ones warm), summed over every job, with each measured machine type's host terms (build/expected_scores.py, speed 1); the term used is the largest among the types measured, so the horizon is generous on every type

measured.source: scripted packed run <run-tag>, speed 1, caps cpus 42 cpuset 2-43 memory 346300m; status completed, jobs_ended
scripted packed run <run-tag>, speed 1, caps cpus 42 cpuset 2-43 memory 346300m; status completed, jobs_ended

environment_floor.how: per machine type: the overlapping packed policy's makespan from agent start (packed_overlap: each successor's start-up runs during its predecessor's GPU work, the runner rule; build/expected_scores.py, speed 1) with the host terms measured on that type at its box's caps and image (`measured`), minus stats.lower_bound_makespan_s. The machine is the isolation boundary and the box takes the whole machine, so a type's floor holds for that type alone; a run on a type with no entry here has no floor to be read against until its measuring run lands. host-terms files are survey/host-terms/<task_id>.<machine type>.json; the fleet's type today is c3-highmem-44

horizon_how: colleague_round(1.5 x (stats.serial_makespan_s + horizon_terms.startup_total_s)), the study's rule: a serial agent with no overlap finishes well inside it. Rounded up to 5 minutes under an hour, 15 minutes under six hours, whole hours above. Never shown to the agent: it is the run's hard stop and the end of the scoring window when work remains. In recorded seconds, like stats: a run with the speed knob divides it by the same factor. One value for every machine type, from the largest measured start-up total (horizon_terms). c3-highmem-44 is measured; a new machine type, caps or image that moves it makes another task version. Replaced deadline_s, which the brief stated, on 2026-10-20; runs under a brief that stated a deadline are not pooled with runs under this one

work_remaining.how: at the horizon, every job without a completed run counts as remaining: not launched, still running, or failed and not rerun to completion. A decision-bound job counts once its slot is known; before that, each unfilled slot counts as one job

python.how: the records carry no Python version; 3.11.9 is one of the two isolation's build.sh pins, torch 2.11.0 has a CPU wheel for it, and the scripts use no version-specific feature (the repo's Dockerfile uses 3.12.7)

install.how: torch 2.11.0 matches the records this task draws (their torch: 2.11.0+cu128, 2.11.0+cu130) and the track's README quickstart (`pip install torch==2.11`). Its runtime dependencies and numpy are pinned in the constraints at their newest final release before 2026-05-01, the records' earliest date, that installs on Python 3.11 (PyPI, read 2026-10-20), except setuptools under 82, because torch 2.11.0 requires it, and mpmath 1.3.0, because sympy 1.14.0 requires mpmath<1.4. Chosen, not recorded: the records hold no package list

environment.hub_how: none: the training data are the Hub dataset's files, placed in the tree by build/stage_task.py (files[] git_lfs entry)
environment.env_how: nothing: the scripts read data/fineweb10B/ relative to the working directory and write logs/<uuid>.txt there
environment.verified: pending: the staging check on the VM (build/check_staging.sh) under these pins; gpu-mock's replay of a track-3 script on torch 2.11 is gpu-mock's own check

image_label.how: one p006.task-env label for every package task drawn from this image, so one image serves the whole package family

task_class_how: no job can use more than 1 of the box's 4 GPUs, so filling the box means running several jobs at once

model_runs.how: allowed when no two jobs can be served the same recorded run or overlapping steps of one (common.repeated_records): a seed-substituted job, two prefix jobs cut from one parent, or a prefix and its parent's full run all repeat losses an agent can see. Scripted runs read no values, so they may run any task

rerun_siblings_how: gpu-mock serves a job's primary record once per run; a later lookup of it by another job key (a rerun) gets the first unused id of that job's rerun_siblings, served by id whatever its bound_path, then the primary again (draw: reused) when the list is spent. Siblings are other recorded runs of the same script and stop step, none overlapping any record any job of the task lists or another job's siblings (build/siblings.py; validate.py checks it). Segments have none: a resumed segment follows the run of the checkpoint it loads (gpu-mock's lineage rule). Evidence that a sibling is a faithful rerun: newton-muon's one script fixes no seed, so its 15 recorded runs are reruns of identical code, and they vary as much at step 250 as other setups do across seeds (survey/siblings-2026-10-21.json, rerun_spread)
